meta.description: Machine-readable public API reference for the current EmptySock engine (bitECS-backed entity/component core, plus the systems in `systems` that never needed a rewrite). Load at agent task start for full typed context. No internal implementation details.

stack.language: TypeScript strict mode recommended; plain JavaScript is fully first-class

banned_patterns: async onUpdate() — type error in TS, runtime warning in JS
JSON.parse(x) as T — always use Zod or a real guard
mutating a networked component field in place (breaks NetworkSystem's dirty-check — reassign instead)
required_patterns: explicit return types on all functions
Zod schema (or equivalent guard) for all external/save data
scene.destroy(entity) when an entity is done — same call whether pooled or not

config.startScene: string — name of first scene to load
config.splash: boolean — show splash on boot, default false

methods.pushScene: Engine.pushScene(scene: Scene): void — push a scene on the stack (mirrors SceneManager.pushScene; use this.engine.pushScene() from inside a Scene)
methods.popScene: Engine.popScene(): void — pop the top scene (use this.engine.popScene() from inside a Scene)
methods.loadScene: Engine.loadScene(name: string): void — load a named scene, replacing the active scene (use this.engine.loadScene() from inside a Scene)

Scene.description: Base class. Extend for every game scene.

static.config: SceneConfig — declare as static readonly on each subclass

SceneConfig.gameSpeed: number — overrides engine default for this scene
SceneConfig.physics: boolean — enable Rapier world, default true
SceneConfig.lighting: boolean — enable 2D lighting pass, default false

lifecycle.onLoad: async onLoad(): Promise<void> — awaited before scene renders
lifecycle.onStart: onStart(): void — called once after onLoad
lifecycle.onUpdate: onUpdate(dt: number): void — every frame, dt = seconds
lifecycle.onPause: onPause(): void — when scene is pushed under another
lifecycle.onResume: onResume(): void — when scene returns to top

methods.createEntity: scene.createEntity(name: string, opts?: { position?: Point, rotation?: number, scale?: Point }): Entity

methods.pushScene: SceneManager.pushScene(scene: Scene): void — push a scene instance on top of the stack; active scene is paused
methods.popScene: SceneManager.popScene(): void — pop top scene; scene underneath resumes

TransitionOptions.duration: number (seconds) — delay before scene switch. Default 0.3

SceneManager.attachPostProcess: SceneManager.attachPostProcess(postProcess: PostProcessSystem): void — wires transition() to drive that PostProcessSystem's transition state via a minimal TransitionEffectSink interface (beginTransition/transitionProgress/endTransition); SceneManager never imports pixi
SceneManager.note_transition_effects: SceneManager only tracks and times the effect — it never touches pixi/DOM. Call attachPostProcess() once, then call RenderPipeline.renderTransitionOverlay(postProcess) (or renderFrame(scene, postProcess)) each frame to paint it: a full-screen overlay rect on top of the current frame, not a true two-scene crossfade.

methods.addComponent: entity.addComponent<T extends Component>(component: T): T — pass an already-constructed instance, e.g. entity.addComponent(new Sprite({...}))
methods.getComponent: entity.getComponent<T>(type: ComponentType<T> | string): T | undefined — built-in components expose a typed token as Sprite.TYPE
methods.on: entity.on(event: string, fn: (data: unknown) => void): void
methods.once: entity.once(event: string, fn: (data: unknown) => void): void
methods.onCollisionEnter: entity.onCollisionEnter(fn: (other: Entity, contact: ContactInfo) => void): void

Sprite.description: Attaching Sprite alongside Transform is all a game needs for an entity to appear on screen — RenderPipeline.renderFrame() finds every Transform+Sprite pair each frame and keeps a PixiJS sprite in sync automatically. There is no separate manual render-registration step.
Sprite.constructor: new Sprite(options?: { texturePath?: string, tint?: number, alpha?: number, anchorX?: number, anchorY?: number, layer?: string, depth?: number, visible?: boolean })
Sprite.staticType: Sprite.TYPE: ComponentType<Sprite> — pass to entity.getComponent()/requireComponent() for a typed lookup

props.depth: number — draw order within layer, lower draws first (behind), default 0

methods.play: animator.play(clip: string, opts?: { loop?: boolean, onComplete?: () => void }): void

PhysicsBody.import: import { PhysicsBody, type CollisionCallback, type SensorCallback, type ContactInfo } from '@emptysock/engine'
PhysicsBody.description: Value component describing the shape and material of a rigid body, and the place to register real collision/sensor callbacks. PhysicsSystem owns the Rapier world and dispatches to these callbacks when it drains real Rapier collision/intersection events each step() — game code registers callbacks but never calls the dispatch* methods itself.
PhysicsBody.constructor: new PhysicsBody(options?: { bodyType?: RigidBodyType, shape?: ColliderShape, width?: number, height?: number, radius?: number, density?: number, friction?: number, restitution?: number, isSensor?: boolean })

props.isSensor: boolean — detect overlaps without generating forces, default false
props.bodyHandle: number | null — Rapier rigid body handle; set by PhysicsSystem.registerEntity(), null until registered
props.colliderHandle: number | null — Rapier collider handle; set by PhysicsSystem.registerEntity(), null until registered

methods.onCollisionEnter: body.onCollisionEnter(cb: (other: PhysicsBody, contact: ContactInfo) => void): void — fires when this body starts touching another (non-sensor) body
methods.onCollisionExit: body.onCollisionExit(cb: (other: PhysicsBody, contact: ContactInfo) => void): void — fires when this body stops touching another (non-sensor) body
methods.onSensorEnter: body.onSensorEnter(cb: (other: PhysicsBody) => void): void — fires when another body enters this sensor
methods.onSensorExit: body.onSensorExit(cb: (other: PhysicsBody) => void): void — fires when another body exits this sensor
methods.onSensorStay: body.onSensorStay(cb: (other: PhysicsBody) => void): void — fires every step while another body remains inside this sensor

ContactInfo.impactForce: number — approximate impact force, in Newtons

PhysicsBody.note: PhysicsSystem._drainCollisionEvents() also still emits entity.emit('collisionEnter'/'collisionExit'/'sensorEnter'/'sensorExit', other) on the entity for the older entity-event path (see skills/03-physics-3d.md's 2D section) — both fire side by side; prefer PhysicsBody.onCollisionEnter()/onSensorEnter() etc. for new code since you already hold the component reference.

RigidJoint.description: Component that constrains two PhysicsBody entities with a Rapier joint. Attach to the entity that holds the first PhysicsBody; set bodyBEntityId to the second entity's numeric id.

props.bodyBEntityId: number | null — entity id of the second body

RevoluteOptions.anchorB: { x, y } — anchor on body B in local space

PrismaticOptions.axis: { x, y } — slide axis in local space of body A

lifecycle.flush: input.flush(): void — call once per frame before reading state

keyMethods.isKeyReleased: input.isKeyReleased(code: string): boolean — true only on the frame the key came up

SaveSystem.description: Generic key-value persistence for save slots, backed by localStorage. All operations are synchronous. Only knows how to store/retrieve/validate an opaque JSON object per slot under a prefixed key — the slot's shape is supplied to the constructor as a Zod schema.
SaveSystem.constructor: new SaveSystem<TSlot = GameSaveSlot>(prefix?: string, schema?: z.ZodType<TSlot>) — with no schema, defaults to the GameSaveSlot shape. schema must validate the full slot including an id: string field; save() fills id in from the slot name automatically. prefix sets the localStorage key prefix, default 'emptysock_save_'.

methods.save: save(slotId: string, entry): void — with the default schema, timestamp defaults to Date.now() and playtime to 0 when omitted, so entry only needs scene and data. Logs a warning and writes nothing if the assembled slot fails validation.
methods.load: load(slotId: string): TSlot | null — returns null for a missing slot, corrupted JSON, or a slot that no longer matches the schema. Never throws. A non-null result is already validated.
methods.listSlots: listSlots(): TSlot[] — every stored slot under this instance's prefix that currently validates; malformed/foreign entries are skipped, not thrown.
methods.delete: delete(slotId: string): void — no-ops if the slot doesn't exist.

methods.setLocale: instance.setLocale(locale: string): void — switch the active locale
methods.addTranslations: instance.addTranslations(locale: string, map: Record<string, string>): void — register translations for a locale
methods.t: instance.t(key: string, vars?: Record<string, string | number>): string — translate key; returns key itself if not found
methods.currentLocale: instance.currentLocale: string — read-only getter for the active locale

methods.setGrid: PathfindingSystem.setGrid(grid: Grid): void — store a grid so subsequent findPath() calls can omit it
methods.findPath: PathfindingSystem.findPath(opts: { from: Point, to: Point, grid?: Grid, allowDiagonal?: boolean }): Promise<Path> — grid is optional if setGrid() was called

TilemapLayer.getTile: layer.getTile(x: number, y: number): Tile | null

ObjectPool.constructor: new ObjectPool<T>(EntityClass: new() => T, opts: { size: number })

ParticleEmitter.description: Component that spawns and animates short-lived visual particles. Attach to an entity, configure options, then call start() or burst().

constructorOptions.rate: number — particles emitted per second in continuous mode
constructorOptions.speed: number — initial speed in world units/second
constructorOptions.spread: number — emission cone half-angle in degrees (0 = straight line, 360 = sphere)
constructorOptions.textureName: string (optional) — asset name for sprite-sheet particles; omit for default white square

methods.start: emitter.start(): void — begin continuous emission at the configured rate
methods.stop: emitter.stop(): void — stop emitting new particles; existing particles finish their lifetime
methods.burst: emitter.burst(count: number): void — fire exactly count particles immediately, ignoring rate

properties.rate: number — read/write, effective before start() is called

notes: Call stop() in onDestroy before the entity is destroyed.
burst() does not require start() to have been called first.
Particles sharing the same textureName are batched into one draw call.
count should be kept as low as visually acceptable — all particles update every frame.

RenderPipeline.import: import { RenderPipeline, type RenderPipelineOptions, type TextureLoader } from '@emptysock/engine'
RenderPipeline.description: The primary, batteries-included way to render a game. Owns a RenderSystem (raw PixiJS renderer) and a LayerSystem (draw order). Every renderFrame(scene) call finds all Transform+Sprite entities, syncs a PixiJS sprite per entity (position, rotation, scale, tint, alpha, anchor, visibility, layer, depth), loads textures once, draws any mounted Tilemap, then renders. Transform+Sprite is the entire contract for "this shows up on screen" — no manual PixiJS wiring.

RenderPipelineOptions.layers: LayerSystem — share an existing LayerSystem instead of creating one
RenderPipelineOptions.textureLoader: TextureLoader — (path: string) => Promise<Texture>; overrides how texture paths resolve, defaults to Assets.load

init.description: Initializes the underlying renderer. Await in onLoad.

renderFrame.description: Sync every Transform+Sprite entity in scene to its PixiJS sprite, then render the frame. Call once per frame after scene update logic. Pass the scene's PostProcessSystem and it also calls renderTransitionOverlay(postProcess) for you.

renderTransitionOverlay.description: Paints SceneManager.transition()'s active effect as a full-screen Graphics overlay on top of the current frame, reading postProcess.transitionEffect/transitionProgress/transitionColour: a triangle-wave alpha for 'fade', a growing rect for 'wipe', a rect sweeping across the screen for 'slide'. No-op when no transition is active. Called automatically by renderFrame() when a PostProcessSystem is passed; call it directly for a custom render loop.

syncEntities.description: Sync PixiJS sprites without rendering — for tests or a custom render loop.

mountTilemap.signature: (tilemap: Tilemap, renderLayer?: string, autoTile?: AutoTileSystem): void
mountTilemap.description: Build real tile sprites for tilemap and add them to renderLayer (default 'default'). Pass an AutoTileSystem to resolve neighbour-aware tile variants. Safe to call once per tilemap.

unmountTilemap.description: Remove a mounted tilemap's sprites. Call before remounting to rebuild after edits.

destroy.description: Required in onDestroy(). Unmounts all tilemaps, destroys all sprites, and destroys the renderer and LayerSystem.

properties.layers: LayerSystem (getter) — call defineLayer() on it for custom draw order

examples: fix(physics): character clips through thin floor at high speed
perf(particles): cap emitter on low GPU tier
chore(assets): compress atlas for Pi export

builtins.description: Compile-time constants injected by the EmptySock build pipeline. Replace with literal values at build time — no runtime lookup. Available in all game files without import.

DEBUG.source: true in debug build, false in release

AutoTileSystem.description: Selects tile variants based on 8-neighbour bitmask rules.

resolve.signature: (col: number, row: number, baseTileIndex: number, tileAt: (col: number, row: number) => number): number
resolve.description: Returns the tile index to paint at (col, row) given neighbour occupancy.

VariableStore.import: import { VariableStore, variableStore, evaluateCondition, type VariableCondition } from '@emptysock/engine'
VariableStore.description: Indexed integer variables (1-1000) and boolean switches (1-1000) with localStorage persistence. Also the home of the shared VariableCondition seam used by VNSystem's condition nodes / choice `when` and MapEventSystem's `when`.

reset.description: Clear all variables to 0 and all switches to false in memory. Does not persist — call save() afterwards if the reset should survive a reload.

VariableStore.singleton: variableStore: VariableStore — module-level shared instance. VNSystem and MapEventSystem both default to it when constructed with no arguments. Pass a separate VariableStore instance to either constructor for isolation (per-save-slot state, tests).
VariableStore.VariableCondition: type VariableCondition = { kind: 'switch', index: number, equals: boolean } | { kind: 'variable', index: number, op: 'eq' | 'neq' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte', value: number }
VariableStore.evaluateCondition: evaluateCondition(store: VariableStore, condition: VariableCondition): boolean — evaluates a VariableCondition against a store's current values.

MapEventSystem.description: Tile-aligned event system with autorun, player-touch, action-button, and parallel trigger types.

update.signature: (playerTileX: number, playerTileY: number, actionPressed: boolean): void

MapEventSystem.constructor: new MapEventSystem(store?: VariableStore) — defaults to the shared variableStore singleton. Used to gate `when`-conditioned events and to apply set-variable/set-switch commands.

MapEvent.when: VariableCondition | undefined — optional gate; when present and false, update() skips the event entirely (never triggers/autoruns/parallels), re-checked every frame.

GridMovementBehavior.description: Smooth 4-directional tile-aligned movement behavior. Attach to an entity via addBehavior().

VNSystem.import: import { VNSystem, type IVNListener, type DialogueNode, type DialogueTree } from '@emptysock/vn'
VNSystem.description: Standalone visual novel runtime. Loads a DialogueTree (converted from Story Graph JSON via storyGraphToDialogueTree). Used by VNTextbox as its data source.
VNSystem.constructor: new VNSystem(store?: VariableStore) — defaults to the shared variableStore singleton. The store backs 'condition' nodes and a choice option's `when` field.
VNSystem.DialogueNode: type DialogueNode = { type: 'dialogue'; speaker: string; text: string; voice?: string; next?: string; cgPath?: string } | { type: 'choice'; text: string; options: Array<{ label: string; next: string; when?: VariableCondition }>; cgPath?: string } | { type: 'event'; eventName: string; data?: Record<string, unknown>; next?: string; cgPath?: string } | { type: 'jump'; target: string; cgPath?: string } | { type: 'variable-set'; variableKey: string; variableValue: unknown; next?: string; cgPath?: string } | { type: 'condition'; condition: VariableCondition; ifTrue: string; ifFalse?: string; cgPath?: string }
VNSystem.DialogueTree: interface DialogueTree { nodes: Record<string, DialogueNode>; startNode: string }

load.description: Load a DialogueTree and begin processing from startNode. Fires onNode immediately for the first node. Not async — use storyGraphToDialogueTree() or JSON.parse() on a fetched file before calling.

advance.description: Advance past a dialogue, event, or variable-set node to its next. Has no effect on choice or jump nodes.

selectOption.description: Navigate to the target node by ID. Use the next field from the chosen option in a choice node.

currentNode.description: The currently active node, or null if not loaded or finished.

setListener.description: Register the active listener. Replaces any previously set listener. Call before load() so the first onNode is delivered.

removeListener.description: Detach the current listener. Subsequent node events are discarded.

getVariable.description: Retrieve the value of a variable set by a 'variable-set' node, or undefined if not yet set.

notes: 'condition' nodes branch to ifTrue/ifFalse based on evaluateCondition(store, condition) and resolve/advance synchronously like jump — onNode never fires for them.
A choice option's `when: VariableCondition` is evaluated against the store before onChoice fires; options that evaluate false are filtered out and never seen by the listener.
Call setListener() before load(). onNode fires immediately on load().
jump nodes are resolved automatically — onNode is never called for them.
variable-set nodes are auto-advanced; read their value with getVariable(key).
No destroy() method — GC'd with the scene when the reference drops.
For save/resume: store currentNode?.id and re-walk the graph on resume.
VNSystem.IVNListener: interface IVNListener { onNode?: (node: DialogueNode) => void; onChoice?: (options: Array<{ label: string; next: string }>) => void; onEvent?: (eventName: string, ...args: unknown[]) => void; onEnd?: () => void; onCGNode?: (cgPath: string) => void }
VNSystem.variables: Map<string, unknown> (readonly) — all variables set by 'variable-set' nodes during playback

VNTextbox.description: Pre-built dialogue box rendered by UISystem. Bind to a VNSystem instance to auto-update. Clicking the textbox automatically calls VNSystem.advance(). Call destroy() in onDestroy.
VNTextbox.constructor: new VNTextbox({ canvasWidth, canvasHeight, height?, namePlateHeight?, paddingX?, panelColor?, namePlateColor?, textColor?, fontSize? })

bind.description: Wire to a VNSystem; immediately syncs to the current node.

destroy.description: Remove textbox from UISystem. Call in onDestroy.

NavMeshSystem.import: import { NavMeshSystem, type NavMeshData, type NavPolygon, type Vec2 } from '@emptysock/engine'
NavMeshSystem.description: A* polygon navmesh for entity pathfinding. Accepts pre-built navmesh data (offline). Does not generate navmesh from tilemaps at runtime.

load.description: Load a pre-built polygon graph. Build this offline in the level editor and ship as a JSON asset.

findPath.description: Find a path between two world-space points. Returns an array of waypoints; returns [] if no path exists. Synchronous.

update.description: Reserved for dynamic obstacle updates. Call once per frame in onUpdate.

NavPolygon.vertices: ReadonlyArray<Vec2> — convex polygon vertices in order
NavPolygon.neighbours: ReadonlyArray<number> — ids of adjacent walkable polygons

notes: NavMesh data is offline — no runtime generation from tilemap data.
Use PathfindingSystem for grid-based A* on a TilemapLayer.asGrid().
NavMeshSystem uses polygon-graph A* and is suited for open-world navigation.

CoroutineSystem.import: import { CoroutineSystem, waitFrames, waitSeconds, waitUntil, type CoroutineGen } from '@emptysock/engine'
CoroutineSystem.description: Lightweight coroutine runner. Drives generator functions over time. Entity.startCoroutine() uses this internally; use CoroutineSystem directly when you need named coroutines outside of an entity context.

start.description: Start a named coroutine. If a coroutine with the same id is already running it is replaced.

stop.description: Stop a running coroutine by name.

update.description: Advance all running coroutines. Call once per frame.

properties.onError: (id: string, error: unknown) => void | null — optional callback invoked when a coroutine throws. Assign directly: coroutines.onError = (id, err) => { ... }

helpers.waitFrames: yield waitFrames(n: number) — pause for n frames
helpers.waitSeconds: yield waitSeconds(t: number) — pause for t seconds
helpers.waitUntil: yield waitUntil(fn: () => boolean) — pause until predicate returns true

GamepadSystem.import: import { GamepadSystem, type GamepadState, type DualRumbleOptions } from '@emptysock/engine'
GamepadSystem.description: Low-level gamepad polling. Wraps the browser Gamepad API. For most input needs, use InputSystem.isKeyDown() / isKeyPressed() instead — they integrate GamepadSystem state internally.

update.description: Poll all connected gamepads. Call once per frame before reading state.

getState.description: Get the current state of gamepad at index (0-based). Returns null if not connected.

rumble.signature: (index: number, intensity: number, duration: number): void
rumble.description: Simple equal-magnitude rumble on both motors.

rumbleDual.description: Independent weak and strong motor rumble.

TweenManager.import: import { TweenManager, type TweenOptions, type EasingName } from '@emptysock/engine'
TweenManager.description: Interpolates numeric properties on objects over time. Also provides scene-local timers. Use one TweenManager per scene; call update(dt) each frame; destroy in onDestroy.

to.signature: (target: Record<string, number>, props: Record<string, number>, options: TweenOptions): void
to.description: Tween numeric properties of target from their current values to the values in props.

after.description: Run fn once after seconds. Scene-local timer managed by this TweenManager.

every.description: Run fn repeatedly every seconds. Continues until the TweenManager is destroyed.

update.description: Advance all active tweens and timers. Call once per frame in onUpdate(dt).

PostProcessSystem.import: import { PostProcessSystem, type PostEffectType, type PostEffectOptions, type LayerFilterOptions } from '@emptysock/engine'
PostProcessSystem.description: Instance-based post-processing pipeline. Create one per scene; call update(dt) each frame for transient effects to decay. Effects are composited in add order.

add.description: Add or replace a full-screen effect. Returns this for method chaining.

remove.description: Remove a full-screen effect by type.

has.description: Whether the effect is currently active.

get.description: Read the current options for an active effect.

flash.description: Transient full-screen flash. colour is a hex number (default 0xffffff); duration in seconds (default 0.15).

setLayerFilter.description: Apply a CSS filter to a named render layer.

clearLayerFilter.description: Remove the filter from a layer.

toggleLayerFilter.description: Enable or disable a layer's filter without removing it.

update.description: Decay transient effects (flash, shockwave). Call once per frame in onUpdate.

clear.description: Remove all effects and reset scene transitions.

destroy.description: Clear all effects and layer filters. Call in onDestroy.

PostProcessSystem.ColourblindMode: 'protanopia' | 'deuteranopia' | 'tritanopia' — used as LayerFilterOptions.mode when filter type is 'colourblind'

transitionProperties.transitionEffect: TransitionEffect — 'none' | 'fade' | 'wipe' | 'slide'; set by SceneManager.transition() through attachPostProcess(), read by RenderPipeline.renderTransitionOverlay()
transitionProperties.transitionProgress: number — 0..1, driven by SceneManager each update()

PostProcessSystem.note_scene_transitions: PostProcessSystem structurally satisfies SceneManager's TransitionEffectSink interface, so passing it to SceneManagerInstance.attachPostProcess() is enough to wire SceneManager.transition({ effect, duration, colour }) through to these three properties — no extra glue code. See docs/manual/21-scene-manager.md and skills/21-post-process.md.
notes: The 'colourblind' layer filter applies standard Brettel/Viénot/Machado *simulation* matrices — it shows a non-colourblind player what a colourblind player sees. It is not a correction/daltonisation filter that increases discriminability for a colourblind player.

LayerSystem.import: import { LayerSystem, LAYER, type LayerConfig, type LayerSortKey } from '@emptysock/engine'
LayerSystem.description: Instance-based named render-layer manager. Entities are assigned to a layer at an explicit depth; RenderSystem draws layers in ascending index order, then entities within a layer by ascending depth. Four built-in layers are pre-created by the constructor.

defineLayer.description: Define or redefine a layer. Lower index = drawn behind. Use index gaps (0, 50, 80, 100) so layers can be inserted later without renumbering.

addEntity.signature: (entityId: number, layerName: string, depth?: number): void
addEntity.description: Assign an entity to a layer at an optional depth (default 0). Unknown layerName falls back to 'default' with a warning.

removeEntity.description: Unregister an entity from the layer system. Entity is not destroyed.

setDepth.description: Update an entity's depth within its current layer without changing the layer.

getEntityLayer.description: Returns the entity's current layer name, or null if unregistered.

getEntityDepth.description: Returns the entity's current depth, or 0 if unregistered.

getSortKey.description: Returns [layerIndex, depth] for use in a sort comparator. Unregistered entities get [LAYER.DEFAULT, 0].

getLayerIndex.description: Returns the index of a named layer, or LAYER.DEFAULT if unknown.

setVisible.description: Show or hide an entire layer.

isVisible.description: Returns true if the layer is visible.

getEntitiesOnLayer.signature: (layerName: string): Array<{ entityId: number; depth: number }>
getEntitiesOnLayer.description: All entities on a layer, sorted by depth ascending.

getLayersSorted.description: All layer configs sorted by index ascending (render order). LayerConfig: { name, index, visible }.

destroy.description: Clear all placements and layers. Call in onDestroy.

notes: Use LAYER constants for the four built-in layer indices.
depth within a layer controls fine-grained draw order within the same layer.
Unregistered entities fallback to [LAYER.DEFAULT, 0] in getSortKey.

ActorSystem.import: import { Actor, ActorSystem, NetworkActor, type Message, type ActorId, type Transport, type TransportMessage } from '@emptysock/engine'
ActorSystem.description: Mailbox-based Actor Model for decoupled game logic. Actors communicate only via messages — no shared mutable state. Create one ActorSystem per scene; destroy it in onDestroy.

Actor.description: Base class for all actors. Extend it and implement receive() and update().

methods.receive: (msg: Message): void — handle an incoming message
methods.update: (dt: number): void — called every frame after all mailboxes are flushed

ActorSystem.description: Manages a set of actors; drains every actor's inbox before calling update() on any actor. Create in onLoad, call update(dt) in onUpdate, call destroy() in onDestroy.

methods.register: (actor: Actor): void — register an actor with the system
methods.unregister: (id: string): void — remove an actor; triggers its onStop() if defined
methods.send: (id: string, msg: Message): void — enqueue a message to a specific actor
methods.broadcast: (msg: Message): void — enqueue a message to all registered actors (O(n))
methods.update: (dt: number): void — flush all mailboxes then call update(dt) on every actor
methods.destroy: (): void — unregister all actors and free resources. Call in onDestroy.
methods.getAll: (): Actor[] — return a snapshot array of all currently registered actors

NetworkActor.description: Opt-in base class for actors that send or receive messages over a network Transport. Extends Actor.

methods.setTransport: (transport: Transport): void — wire a Transport implementation
methods.sendRemote: (channel: string, msg: Message): void — forward a message through the Transport

Transport.description: Interface. The engine ships no concrete Transport. Implement it in game code and inject at runtime.

notes: Messages sent inside an actor's receive() are processed in the same flush pass — not deferred to the next frame.
An actor that always re-enqueues a message to itself in receive() creates an infinite flush loop.
Use targeted send() for high-frequency messages; broadcast() is O(n).
Create a new ActorSystem in onLoad and destroy it in onDestroy to avoid stale-actor bugs across scene transitions.

PhysicsSystem3D.description: Full Rapier3D integration for 3D physics. WASM-based — must call await physics.init() before adding bodies. Always call physics.destroy() in onDestroy to free WASM memory.

init.signature: (gravity: { x: number, y: number, z: number }): Promise<void>
init.description: Initialise the Rapier3D WASM world with the given gravity vector. Must be awaited before calling addBody.

addBody.description: Add a rigid body to the simulation. Returns a handle for reading position/rotation and applying forces.

removeBody.description: Remove a body from the simulation by its bodyIndex.

update.description: Step the physics simulation. Call once per frame in onUpdate.

destroy.description: Free all WASM-allocated physics memory. Required in onDestroy — the GC cannot see WASM memory.

Body3DOptions.halfExtents: { x, y, z } — for box shape
Body3DOptions.radius: number — for sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone
Body3DOptions.isSensor: boolean (optional) — detect overlaps without generating forces

Body3DHandle.getPosition: (): { x: number, y: number, z: number }
Body3DHandle.getRotation: (): { x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number }
Body3DHandle.applyImpulse: (impulse: { x: number, y: number, z: number }): void

notes: Always await physics.init() before adding bodies — Rapier WASM must initialise first.
Always call physics.destroy() in onDestroy — WASM memory is outside the JS heap and the GC cannot free it.
Sensor bodies (isSensor: true) detect overlaps without generating physical response forces.

PluginSystem.import: import { pluginSystem, type Plugin, type PluginContext } from '@emptysock/engine'
PluginSystem.description: Module-level singleton for registering process-global engine extensions. Plugins install optional services (analytics, ads, platform achievements) once for the app lifetime. The singleton is shared across all scenes — no per-scene construction needed.
PluginSystem.singleton: pluginSystem — import and use directly; do not construct a new PluginSystem

register.description: Register a plugin and call its install() method. Throws if a plugin with the same name is already registered.

unregister.description: Call the plugin's uninstall() method and remove it from the registry.

inject.description: Retrieve a value provided by a plugin via ctx.provide(). Returns undefined if no plugin provided the key.

properties.registeredPlugins: readonly string[] — names of all currently registered plugins

Plugin.name: string — unique plugin name; duplicate registration throws

PluginContext.provide: (key: string, value: unknown): void — expose a value for pluginSystem.inject()

notes: pluginSystem is a module-level singleton — do not construct one per scene.
install() may be async; await pluginSystem.register() to ensure it has completed.
The singleton makes inject() callable from anywhere without passing a reference.

BattleSystem.import: import { BattleSystem, type BattlePhase, type BattleStats, type BattleStatMap, type DamageContext, type StatusEffect, type Combatant, type SkillTargetType, type DamageFormulaId, type SkillDef, type StatusEffectDef, type BattleDatabase, type BattleAction, type BattleEvent, type BattleSystemOptions } from '@emptysock/engine'
BattleSystem.description: Opt-in turn-based RPG battle module. Handles turn order (speed desc), damage resolution, status effects, and event emission. Tree-shaken from bundles that do not import it. Enemies act automatically (attack lowest-HP party member); party members require submitAction(). Public surface is intentionally narrow: start() begins a battle, submitAction() is the only way to advance it, subscribe() is the only way to observe it.

BattleSystemOptions.db: BattleDatabase — optional, can also be loaded via loadDatabase()

setDamageFormula.description: Override the default physical damage formula. ctx gives effectiveAttack/effectiveDefense (already incorporating status multipliers), power, isCrit, critMultiplier, and the full attacker/target Combatants.

start.signature: (party: readonly Combatant[], enemies: readonly Combatant[]): void
start.description: Begin a battle with the given roster, replacing any previous one. Replaces the old addPartyMember()/addEnemy() calls. Fires battle-start, then round-start, then action-needed for the first combatant in turn order.

submitAction.description: Submit a party member's action. Only valid when getPhase() === 'input'. Once every party member submits, the round resolves automatically.

subscribe.description: Subscribe to battle events. Returns an unsubscribe function. Replaces the old onEvent() name.

destroy.description: Required in onDestroy(). Clears all combatants, pending actions, and event listeners.

types.BattleStats: { hp, maxHp, mp, maxMp, attack, defense, speed, luck: number } — built-in fields; see BattleStatMap for user-defined stats
types.BattleStatMap: Record<string, number> — extends the built-in BattleStats with any user-defined stat names. Add extra keys to Combatant.stats; guard reads with ?? 0 in formulas.
types.DamageContext: { attacker: Combatant; defender: Combatant; skill: SkillDef | null } — passed as sixth argument to the setDamageFormula callback
types.StatusEffect: { id: string; name: string; turnsRemaining: number } — turnsRemaining -1 = permanent
types.Combatant: { id: string; name: string; stats: BattleStatMap; statusEffects: readonly StatusEffect[]; isParty: boolean }
types.SkillDef: { id, name, mpCost, targetType: SkillTargetType, formula: DamageFormulaId, power: number, isHeal?: boolean, statusEffect?: { effectId: string; chance: number } }
types.StatusEffectDef: { id, name, hpDrainPercentPerTurn?: number, attackMultiplier?: number, defenseMultiplier?: number }
types.BattleAction: { type: 'attack'; targetId: string } | { type: 'skill'; skillId: string; targetId: string } | { type: 'flee' }
types.BattleEvent: { kind: 'battle-start' } | { kind: 'round-start'; round: number } | { kind: 'action-needed'; combatantId: string } | { kind: 'damage'; sourceId: string; targetId: string; amount: number; isCrit: boolean } | { kind: 'heal'; sourceId: string; targetId: string; amount: number } | { kind: 'mp-cost'; combatantId: string; amount: number } | { kind: 'status-applied'; combatantId: string; effectId: string; name: string } | { kind: 'status-expired'; combatantId: string; effectId: string } | { kind: 'combatant-defeated'; combatantId: string } | { kind: 'victory' } | { kind: 'defeat' } | { kind: 'fled' }

ViewportSystem.import: import { ViewportSystem, computeViewportSize, gpuTierRenderDefaults, type ScaleMode, type ViewportConfig, type ViewportSize, type SafeAreaInsets } from '@emptysock/engine'
ViewportSystem.description: Design-resolution scaling (fit/fill/stretch), window resize + orientation-change listening, and safe-area-inset exposure. Feeds resize() on a render target (RenderSystem or RenderPipeline) and CameraSystem.setViewSize() so they never go stale after the container changes size. The singleton export is `viewportSystem`; games may also construct their own instance.

init.signature: (config: Partial<ViewportConfig>, systems?: { renderTarget?: ResizableRenderTarget, cameraSystem?: CameraSystem }): void
init.description: Wires the render target and CameraSystem to keep in sync, starts resize/orientation listeners, and computes the initial viewport size. Call once in onLoad.

recompute.description: Recomputes the letterboxed/filled/stretched size and pushes it to the render target and CameraSystem. Called automatically on resize/orientation-change.

setDesignResolution.description: Change the design resolution and recompute.

getSafeAreaInsets.description: Reads CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) via a hidden probe element. Returns all-zero insets outside a browser or on platforms without notch/home-indicator insets.

destroy.description: Removes all listeners. Call in onDestroy.

ViewportConfig.designWidth: number — logical width the game is authored against
ViewportConfig.designHeight: number — logical height the game is authored against
ViewportConfig.container: HTMLElement — optional; falls back to window dimensions

ViewportSize.width: number — rendered canvas width in CSS pixels
ViewportSize.height: number — rendered canvas height in CSS pixels
ViewportSize.scale: number — scale factor from design resolution to rendered size

ViewportSystem.ScaleMode: 'fit' | 'fill' | 'stretch' — fit letterboxes (never crops), fill cover-crops (never letterboxes), stretch fills exactly with no aspect correction

functions.computeViewportSize: (designWidth: number, designHeight: number, availableWidth: number, availableHeight: number, scaleMode: ScaleMode): ViewportSize — pure function, safe to unit test without a DOM
functions.gpuTierRenderDefaults: (tier: GPUTier, devicePixelRatio?: number): { antialias: boolean, resolution: number } — GPU-tier-appropriate defaults; pass the result's fields into RenderSystem/RenderPipeline init options

PointerSystem.import: import { PointerSystem, MIN_TOUCH_TARGET_SIZE, type PointerState, type Gesture, type GestureType, type SwipeDirection, type WheelEventInfo } from '@emptysock/engine'
PointerSystem.description: Unifies mouse, touch, and pen input into a single pointer stream using native Pointer Events, plus a dependency-free gesture recognizer (tap / long-press / swipe / pinch) and wheel/trackpad classification. Pair with InputSystem (keyboard/mouse buttons) and GamepadSystem (controllers), not as a replacement for either.

attach.description: Attach native pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup/pointercancel/wheel listeners. Defaults to window. No-op outside a browser-like environment.

detach.description: Remove listeners and clear tracked pointers.

destroy.description: Alias for detach(). Call in onDestroy.

update.description: Call once per frame to poll for long-press (time-based gesture).

onGesture.description: Fires for tap, longpress, swipe, and pinch gestures.

properties.primaryPointer: PointerState | undefined — mouse, or the first active touch

PointerSystem.Gesture: TapGesture | LongPressGesture | SwipeGesture | PinchGesture, discriminated by `type`

WheelEventInfo.isPinchZoom: boolean — true for a trackpad pinch-to-zoom gesture

constants.MIN_TOUCH_TARGET_SIZE: 44 — minimum recommended touch-target size in CSS pixels; pair with UISystem.setScale() for touch-target scaling

AnimatorController.import: import { AnimatorController, type AnimParamValue, type AnimTransitionOptions, type ActiveClipFrame } from '@emptysock/engine'
AnimatorController.description: Code-first animation state machine component: named states (each backed by an AnimationClip), parameter/trigger-gated transitions, and optional linear cross-fade blending. A separate component from the single-clip `Animator`, which is unchanged — use Animator for simple sprite-flipbook playback and AnimatorController when animation depends on named states and parameters (e.g. 'idle'/'run'/'jump' gated on a speed float and a grounded bool).

addState.description: Register a named state backed by a clip.

addTransition.description: Register a transition. Pass '*' as `from` to match from any state.

setTrigger.description: Arms a trigger; stays armed until a transition condition consumes it or resetTrigger() is called.

play.description: Jump straight into a state with no transition/blend, e.g. on setup.

getActiveClips.description: Clip(s)/frame(s)/weight(s) to composite this frame — one entry normally, two during a cross-fade with weights summing to 1.

AnimTransitionOptions.duration: number — optional cross-fade duration in seconds; 0 (default) is an instant cut

AssetManifest.import: import { AssetManifest, type AssetDescriptor, type AssetType, type AssetLoadResult, type AssetLoadFailure } from '@emptysock/engine'
AssetManifest.description: Declarative asset preloader with progress reporting and per-asset failure handling. Loaded textures and audio warm the same caches RenderPipeline and AudioSystem read from, so gameplay code that touches them afterwards does not trigger a redundant fetch. The engine never renders a loading screen itself — build one in your own start scene and drive it from onProgress().

AssetManifestOptions.textureLoader: TextureLoader — optional; pass the same loader given to RenderPipelineOptions.textureLoader so a preloaded texture lands in the identical cache
AssetManifestOptions.audioSystem: AudioSystem — optional; required to load 'audio' type descriptors
AssetManifestOptions.fetchImpl: typeof fetch — optional, defaults to global fetch; injectable for tests
AssetManifestOptions.continueOnError: boolean — default true; when false, load() rejects on the first failure instead of continuing

onProgress.signature: (listener: (loaded: number, total: number, current: AssetDescriptor) => void): () => void
onProgress.description: Subscribe to progress; returns an unsubscribe function.

load.description: Loads every registered asset in order. Per-asset failures are collected in `failures` rather than rejecting the batch, unless continueOnError is false.

AssetDescriptor.id: string — cache key, and AudioSystem sound id for audio assets

InputBindings.import: import { InputBindings, createBindingsSaveSystem, BindingsSaveSlotSchema, type ActionMap, type Binding, type BindingsSaveSlot } from '@emptysock/engine'
InputBindings.description: Named-action control remapping layered over InputSystem/GamepadSystem. Games should query `bindings.isActionActive('jump')` rather than a raw key code so players can rebind controls without gameplay code branching on physical keys. Persisted via SaveSystem's generic schema API, not the default save slot shape.
InputBindings.constructor: new InputBindings(input: InputSystem, defaults: ActionMap, gamepad?: GamepadSystem | null)

isActionActive.description: True if any binding for the action is currently active (held).

isActionPressed.description: True the frame a key-bound action transitions from inactive to active. Gamepad/mouse bindings do not support edge detection at this layer.

rebind.description: Replace all bindings for an action.

save.description: Persist current bindings via a SaveSystem<BindingsSaveSlot> (e.g. from createBindingsSaveSystem()).

load.description: Returns true if persisted bindings were found and applied.

functions.createBindingsSaveSystem: (prefix?: string): SaveSystem<BindingsSaveSlot> — a SaveSystem pre-configured with the bindings slot schema

InputBindings.Binding: KeyBinding | MouseButtonBinding | GamepadButtonBinding | GamepadAxisBinding, discriminated by `kind`

DebugOverlaySystem.import: import { DebugOverlaySystem, type DebugLogEntry, type LogLevel } from '@emptysock/engine'
DebugOverlaySystem.description: Shippable in-game FPS/entity-count overlay and dev console, disabled by default. Renders through the existing UI widget tree (PanelWidget + LabelWidget), so add its `root` widget to a scene's UISystem — no separate rendering path.

update.description: Call once per frame with delta time and current entity count.

logError.description: Intended to be wired to the engine's error hook so runtime errors surface in-overlay.

registerCommand.signature: (name: string, handler: (args: string[]) => string | void): void
registerCommand.description: Register a console command. 'help' and 'clear' are registered by default.

runCommand.description: Parses 'name arg1 arg2' and dispatches to a registered command.

properties.root: PanelWidget — add to a scene's UISystem

AccessibilitySettings.description: Module-level singleton (like pluginSystem) holding a global text-scale multiplier that every LabelWidget reads at render time — a settings-menu slider can affect all on-screen text without threading a prop through every widget's constructor.

VisualScriptComponent.import: import { VisualScriptComponent, VisualScriptGraphBuilder, type VisualScriptGraph } from '@emptysock/engine'
VisualScriptComponent.description: ECS Component that holds a serialized node graph and interprets it each frame or on a fired event — the runtime counterpart to the Visual Script Editor panel, which authors the same VisualScriptGraph shape.
VisualScriptComponent.constructor: new VisualScriptComponent(options: { graph: VisualScriptGraph, variableStore?: VariableStore, actorSystem?: ActorSystem }) — variableStore defaults to a private instance; actorSystem is required only if the graph contains sendMessage nodes
VisualScriptComponent.staticType: VisualScriptComponent.TYPE: ComponentType<VisualScriptComponent> — the string "VisualScript" used as the ComponentType key by addComponent/getComponent

nodeTypes.onUpdate: Entry point, fires every update() call
nodeTypes.onEvent: Entry point, fires when fireEvent(eventType) is called — fields: eventType
nodeTypes.branch: Reads a VariableStore variable and compares it — fields: variableIndex, comparator ('eq'|'neq'|'gt'|'lt'|'gte'|'lte'), value; next[0] = true edge, next[1] = false edge
nodeTypes.getVariable: Reads a VariableStore variable into the per-tick evaluation scope — fields: variableIndex, outputKey
nodeTypes.setVariable: Writes a literal or a scoped value into VariableStore — fields: variableIndex, value: number | { fromKey: string }
nodeTypes.getSwitch: Same as getVariable for VariableStore boolean switches — fields: switchIndex, outputKey
nodeTypes.setSwitch: Same as setVariable for VariableStore boolean switches — fields: switchIndex, value
nodeTypes.sendMessage: Sends a real Message through ActorSystem.send() — fields: targetActorId, messageType, payload?

VisualScriptComponent.note_next: Every node carries a next: string[] array of node ids it wires forward to (execution-output ports). branch is the only node with two ports; every other node kind uses next[0].
VisualScriptComponent.VisualScriptGraphBuilder: Produces the exact VisualScriptGraph shape the panel round-trips, for hand-authoring a graph in code. Methods mirror node kinds: b.onUpdate(), b.onEvent(eventType), b.branch(variableIndex, comparator, value), b.setVariable(variableIndex, value), b.getVariable(variableIndex, outputKey), b.setSwitch(switchIndex, value), b.getSwitch(switchIndex, outputKey), b.sendMessage(targetActorId, messageType, payload?) — each returns a node id. b.connect(fromId, toId, port?: 0 | 1) wires an edge (port only meaningful for branch). b.build(): VisualScriptGraph.

methods.update: vs.update(deltaTime: number): void — runs every onUpdate node's chain once. Not async — see the engine-wide 'onUpdate must not be async' rule.
methods.fireEvent: vs.fireEvent(eventType: string): void — runs every onEvent node whose eventType matches
methods.setGraph: vs.setGraph(graph: VisualScriptGraph): void — swap the graph
methods.setActorSystem: vs.setActorSystem(actorSystem: ActorSystem): void — wire an ActorSystem after construction

properties.variableStore: VariableStore — the live store the interpreter is bound to

VisualScriptComponent.note_execution: A trigger fires and execution walks next edges synchronously node-by-node until a node has no outgoing edge for the taken port. A per-tick evaluation scope (cleared at the start of each trigger) lets getVariable/getSwitch results flow into a later setVariable via { fromKey }. A defensive step cap (10,000 steps per trigger) stops a graph wired back into itself from hanging the frame — it logs a warning and returns rather than looping forever, mirroring the ActorSystem mailbox-drain guidance.

CustomShaderFilter.import: import { createCustomShaderFilter, DEFAULT_CUSTOM_SHADER_VERTEX, type CustomShaderFilterOptions } from '@emptysock/engine'
CustomShaderFilter.description: A user-authored GLSL post-process filter — the runtime counterpart to the IDE's ShaderEditor panel. A shader written and previewed there compiles through this exact function, so the panel's preview and a game's actual render use one shader-compile path.

uniformContract.vertexUniforms: uProjectionMatrix, uWorldTransformMatrix, uTransformMatrix (mat3) — standard PixiJS v8 filter uniforms, the same ones LightingFilter uses
uniformContract.fragmentUniforms: uTexture (sampler2D, the filtered input), uTime (float, seconds — update it yourself via setTime())

CustomShaderFilter.note_glsl: Shaders are GLSL ES 3.00 style (in/out, not attribute/varying; texture(), not texture2D()).

functions.createCustomShaderFilter: createCustomShaderFilter(options: { fragmentSrc: string, vertexSrc?: string }): Filter — vertexSrc defaults to DEFAULT_CUSTOM_SHADER_VERTEX. The returned Filter has setTime(seconds: number): void.

CustomShaderFilter.usage: renderSystem.addLayerShaderFilter(layerName: string, filter: Filter): void attaches the filter to a named layer's container; renderSystem.removeLayerShaderFilter(layerName: string, filter: Filter): void detaches it. Both live on RenderSystem (exported standalone from '@emptysock/engine'), not on RenderPipeline. Call filter.setTime(elapsedSeconds) each frame if the shader reads uTime.

SequenceSystem.import: import { TweenManager, SequenceSystem, evaluateTrackAt, type SequenceDefinition, type SequenceTrackDef, type SequenceKeyframe } from '@emptysock/engine'
SequenceSystem.description: Plays a keyframe SequenceDefinition — a list of tracks, each a target property plus keyframes and an optional easing — against a plain numeric target object, by scheduling real TweenManager.to() calls. This is the runtime the IDE's Sequence Editor panel drives; a sequence exported from the panel and a hand-written TweenManager chain produce identical playback, because play() schedules exactly the calls a developer would write by hand.

types.SequenceTrackDef: { property: string, keyframes: SequenceKeyframe[], ease?: EasingName }  — property is a key set on the target object, e.g. 'x', 'rotation'; ease defaults to 'linear'

methods.play: seq.play(tweens: TweenManager, target: Record<string, number>, def: SequenceDefinition, startAt?: number): void — sets target[property] to the exact value at startAt immediately, then schedules one to() per remaining keyframe segment with delay measured from startAt, so resuming mid-playback doesn't jump
methods.stop: seq.stop(): void — cancels all scheduled tweens

SequenceSystem.evaluateTrackAt: evaluateTrackAt(track: SequenceTrackDef, time: number): number — a pure, side-effect-free evaluation of a single track at an arbitrary time, using the same per-segment easing math play() schedules; useful for scrubbing/preview without touching a TweenManager instance

v2.description: The current entity/component/scene core. Everything here lives directly under @emptysock/engine.

defineComponent.signature: defineComponent<T extends SerializableRecord>(componentName: string, createDefaults: () => T, options?: { version?: number; schema?: ComponentSchema<T> }): ComponentDef<T>
defineComponent.notes: componentName is the real identity key (survives hot-reload, where the module re-evaluating produces a new object reference for 'the same' component). Fields must be Serializable — string/number/boolean/null/arrays/plain objects of the same, no functions or class instances.

definePrefab.signature: definePrefab<T>(prefabName: string, components: { def: ComponentDef; overrides?: Partial<T> }[], options?: { extends?: PrefabDef[] }): PrefabDef<T>
definePrefab.notes: extends flattens other prefabs onto the same entity at spawn time, depth-first; a prefab's own components win on a name collision against anything it extends.
definePrefab.example: const Enemy = definePrefab('Enemy', [{ def: Health, overrides: { max: 50 } }], { extends: [Physical] })

properties.rawId: number — raw id, version bits stripped, for logging only
properties.isAlive: boolean — false once destroyed/stale; note: a pooled-and-destroyed entity stays true, see SpawnOptions.pool

methods.add: add<T>(def: ComponentDef<T>, overrides?: Partial<T>): T — throws on a destroyed entity or a component already present
methods.get: get<T>(def: ComponentDef<T>): T | undefined — cached proxy onto the live field arrays
methods.remove: remove<T>(def: ComponentDef<T>): void — no-op if stale or absent

methods.spawn_prefab: spawn<T>(prefab: PrefabDef<T>, props?: Partial<T>, options?: { pool?: boolean }): Entity
methods.destroy: destroy(entity: Entity): void — deallocates, or returns to the prefab's pool if spawned with { pool: true }
methods.each: each<T extends ComponentDef[]>(...defs: T, callback: (...values, entity: Entity) => void): void — bulk iteration, no per-entity proxy allocation

methods.loadScene: loadScene(definition: SceneDefinition, options?: { manageLifecycle?: boolean; physics?: PhysicsInitOptions }): Promise<SceneLifecycle>
methods.loadOverlay: loadOverlay(definition: SceneDefinition, options?: { manageLifecycle?: boolean; physics?: PhysicsInitOptions }): Promise<SceneLifecycle> — no PhysicsSystem unless options.physics is passed
methods.unloadOverlay: unloadOverlay(scene?: Scene): Promise<void> — defaults to the most recently loaded overlay
methods.update: update(dt: number): void — runs the fixed per-frame order: input snapshot, actor flush, physics step, onUpdate, render

defineScene.notes: Prefer this over a bare object literal — it rejects an accidentally-async onUpdate at the type level, which a plain object literal's contextual typing would otherwise let slip through.

SceneDefinition.onUpdate: (dt: number) => void — must not return a Promise

methods.get: get<T>(ctor: new () => T): T — throws if never registered

SaveSystem.constructor: new SaveSystem(scene: Scene, components: ComponentDef[], options?: { adapter?: StorageAdapter; keyPrefix?: string })

methods.registerMigration: registerMigration(componentName: string, migrate: (oldData, oldVersion: number) => SerializableRecord): void

SaveSystem.notes: Defaults to an in-memory StorageAdapter (nothing persists) unless a real one is injected by the host app (IndexedDB in browser preview, Tauri fs on desktop).

PhysicsBody.notes: Plain-language wrapper over Rapier. Collision/sensor callbacks (onCollisionEnter, onCollisionExit, onSensorEnter, onSensorExit, onSensorStay) are assigned directly as properties — assigning is registering.

@emptysock/network.notes: Networked fields must be reassigned as a whole new value on change, never mutated in place — NetworkSystem.sync()'s dirty-check uses strict equality against the last-sent value.

@emptysock/vn.notes: VNSystem's constructor defaults to the engine's global variableStore singleton — pass your own VariableStore instance to isolate a VN's switches/variables from the rest of the game.

@emptysock/tilemap.notes: NavMeshSystem.load() takes a pre-built polygon graph — there is no runtime tilemap-to-navmesh generation. Build it offline (level editor or a preprocessing step).
